description: How to start any system design problem: Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements, Constraints, Assumptions, Traffic, and System Boundaries.

topics.title: Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)
topics.definition: Functional Requirements (FR) define WHAT a system must do (features, user actions, business workflows). Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) define HOW WELL the system must perform (availability, latency, consistency, scalability, durability, security).
topics.why_we_need_it: A system that correctly stores a tweet (FR) but takes 15 seconds to load and crashes every Friday (failed NFR) is an engineering failure. Senior system design interviews are 80% about solving NFRs.
topics.real_world_analogy: Buying an automobile: Functional requirement is that it drives from Point A to Point B with 4 passengers. Non-functional requirements are fuel efficiency (35 MPG), top speed (120 MPH), safety rating (5-star crash durability), and maintenance intervals (every 10,000 miles).
topics.how_it_works: In the first 5 minutes of any system design discussion, you must explicitly partition the problem space into two clear lists: 3-5 core Functional use-cases and 4-5 measurable Non-Functional targets.
conceptual_breakdown: Functional Scope (FR): User post creation, timeline feed retrieval, user search, follow graph, push notifications.
High Availability (NFR): System must achieve 99.99% uptime (~52 minutes downtime per year).
Low Latency (NFR): p99 read latency < 100ms for timeline rendering; p99 write latency < 500ms for post ingestion.
Eventual vs Strong Consistency (NFR): Timelines can tolerate 2-3 seconds of replication lag (Eventual Consistency), but credit card billing requires Strong Consistency.

nodes.name: NFR: 100% Durability
nodes.why: Never lose user data once ACKed

system_flow_animation.title: Balancing FRs with Strict NFR Latency Budgets

steps.description: FR Execution: User requests Timeline Feed (GET /feed).
NFR Enforcement: Request hits Redis timeline cache to satisfy < 100ms p99 latency SLA.
NFR Enforcement: Multi-AZ load balancer guarantees 99.99% availability even if Zone A is offline.
Result: Functional requirement delivered while strictly meeting all Non-Functional SLAs.

topics.tradeoffs: You cannot maximize all NFRs simultaneously. For example, guaranteeing absolute Strong Consistency (ACID across regions) increases write latency and decreases availability during network partitions (CAP theorem).

comparison_matrix.title: Core Non-Functional Requirements Spectrum
rows: Redundant active-active instances across multiple Availability Zones
Distributed in-memory caching (Redis), CDNs, and read replicas
Asynchronous task queues (Kafka) and Write-Ahead Logging
Multi-region Erasure Coding and 3x replica storage (Amazon S3)

topics.failure_scenarios: Failing to define NFRs upfront: designing a payment system with eventual consistency that double-charges customers, or designing a chat app with synchronous SQL queries that freezes under 10,000 active group chats.

common_mistakes.mistake: Listing 25 functional features during an interview instead of focusing on the top 3-4 core workflows
common_mistakes.correction: Deep-dive into 3 core use cases. Interviewers evaluate architectural depth, not exhaustive feature lists.

interview_questions.question: How do you handle conflicting NFRs like ultra-low latency vs strong data consistency?
interview_questions.answer: Explicitly identify which data requires strict consistency (e.g. financial balances require CP) versus data that thrives on low latency with eventual consistency (e.g. video view counters, social feeds). Apply different architectural pipelines to each.

topics.title: Establishing Constraints, Assumptions, Users & Actors
topics.definition: The technique of establishing explicit mathematical scale, traffic boundaries, user demographics, hardware constraints, and out-of-scope agreements to eliminate ambiguity.
topics.why_we_need_it: Vague questions like 'Design Netflix' can mean designing the video encoding pipeline, the recommendation machine learning model, the billing engine, or the content delivery network. Establishing constraints scopes the problem to a solvable engineering goal.
topics.real_world_analogy: A defense contractor building a military vehicle: before designing, they must know if it operates in desert heat (-10°C to +50°C), aquatic rivers, or urban roads, and whether ammunition weight is 500kg or 5,000kg.
topics.how_it_works:
Actively state reasonable assumptions and confirm them with the interviewer:

  • 'I assume our target is 100 million Daily Active Users with a 10:1 Read-to-Write ratio.'
  • 'I assume video files are up to 4K resolution with an average duration of 10 minutes.'
  • 'I will treat user recommendation ML algorithms as an external black-box service and focus on video ingestion, encoding, storage, and streaming CDN delivery.'
conceptual_breakdown: Actors: Creators (uploaders), Consumers (viewers), Moderators (admins), Automated Systems (billing cron, transcoders).
Hard Constraints: Maximum upload size (2 GB), network bandwidth budget, legal data compliance (GDPR in EU).
Out of Scope: Explicitly agreeing on features NOT to build in this 45-minute session to avoid wasting time.

nodes.name: Ad Bidding / Payment Engine
nodes.why: Agreed out of scope to preserve focus

steps.description: Creator uploads 1GB video file via resumable HTTP multipart upload.
System transcodes video into 360p, 720p, 1080p, 4K HLS chunked streams.
100,000 Viewers stream chunks simultaneously from Edge CDN with zero origin server strain.

topics.tradeoffs: Designing for an overly broad scope results in shallow box-drawing. Designing for a tightly scoped set of constraints allows deep architectural exploration of bottlenecks and failure handling.

comparison_matrix.title: System Actors and Workload Characteristics
rows: Audit trail consistency over raw speed

topics.failure_scenarios: Assuming an unlimited upload size without constraints: a single user uploading a 500 GB file consumes all server memory and disk space, starving other users (Denial of Service).

common_mistakes.mistake: Silently making assumptions in your head without stating them to the interviewer
common_mistakes.correction: Always vocalize your assumptions clearly and ask: 'Does this scale match your expectations for this problem?'

interview_questions.question: How do you handle an interviewer who refuses to answer your clarifying questions and says 'You decide'?
interview_questions.answer: State: 'Understood. In that case, I will assume a large-scale global service with 50M DAU, 10:1 read/write ratio, and 99.99% availability target. If our time allows, I will show how the architecture adapts if these constraints change.'

topics.title: System Boundaries, Core APIs & Data Contracts
topics.definition: The practice of creating formal input/output contracts (APIs) and defining data entity schemas before designing internal storage and microservice topologies.
topics.why_we_need_it: APIs and Data Schemas represent the non-negotiable contract between your system and the outside world. Designing the API first (API-First Design) ensures the architecture directly satisfies real user use cases.
topics.real_world_analogy: Ordering goods in international shipping: the standardized shipping container dimensions (20ft / 40ft ISO standards) dictate crane designs, cargo ship layouts, and highway truck trailers worldwide.
topics.how_it_works: Translate functional requirements directly into clean RESTful endpoints or gRPC Protobuf definitions with explicit request payloads, response codes, and query parameters.
conceptual_breakdown: API Signature: HTTP Method + URL path + Query parameters + Request Headers (Authorization, Idempotency-Key).
Data Contract: Strict JSON / Protobuf schema with field types, required/optional flags, and validation rules.

nodes.name: Entity: Video Metadata
nodes.failure: Stored in PostgreSQL with read replicas

nodes.name: Entity: Video Chunks
nodes.failure: Stored in S3 with 11 Nines durability

steps.description: Client invokes POST /api/v1/videos/upload with video title and size metadata.
Gateway validates authorization token and payload schema against API Contract.
System issues Presigned S3 Upload URL to client. Binary video stream uploads directly to S3 without passing through API servers!

topics.tradeoffs: Streaming heavy file uploads through backend API servers burns CPU and network bandwidth. Using presigned object storage URLs offloads massive binary traffic directly to S3.

comparison_matrix.title: API Protocols for System Boundaries
rows: Complex dashboards requiring custom field selection in 1 request
Bi-directional real-time chat & live market feeds

topics.failure_scenarios: Failing to version APIs (`/api/v1/` vs `/api/`): when you change a field name from `userId` to `user_id`, millions of legacy mobile apps in the wild crash instantly upon updating.

common_mistakes.mistake: Jumping into database schema design before establishing the public API endpoints
common_mistakes.correction: Define the API endpoints first. APIs define how the system is used; the database schema is an internal implementation detail that supports the API.

interview_questions.question: How do you design a file upload API for a 20 GB video file without exhausting web server memory?
interview_questions.answer: Use a two-step API: 1. `POST /videos/upload-session` creates a metadata record and returns a Presigned S3 Multipart Upload URL. 2. The client uploads 5MB chunks directly from the browser to Amazon S3 via S3's Multipart API. The API servers never touch the raw video bytes.

topics.title: Interview Case Walkthrough: Scoping 'Design YouTube' from Scratch
topics.definition: A step-by-step masterclass demonstrating the exact dialogue, mathematical scoping, and requirement extraction for a top-tier FAANG interview problem: 'Design YouTube'.
topics.why_we_need_it: Provides learners with a concrete template they can replicate in real interviews to convert an ambiguous 2-word prompt into a structured, production-ready system design blueprint.
topics.real_world_analogy: A courtroom trial opening statement: establishing the exact facts, scope, and boundaries before presenting the detailed evidence.
topics.how_it_works:
Follow the 5-phase opening formula:

  1. Clarification (2 mins): Clarify core features (Upload, Watch, Search). Confirm out of scope (Comments, Live streaming).
  2. Functional Requirements (2 mins): 3 core FRs.
  3. Non-Functional Requirements (2 mins): Availability (99.99%), Latency (Smooth playback, < 200ms start), Durability (Zero video loss).
  4. Capacity & Scale Estimation (3 mins): 1B DAU, 5B video views/day, 50M uploads/day, compute QPS, Storage & CDN egress bandwidth.
  5. High-Level Architecture (5 mins): Draw the block diagram.
conceptual_breakdown: Functional Scope: 1. Upload Video, 2. Stream/Watch Video, 3. Search Video by Title.
Scale Numbers: 1B DAU • 5 Billion views/day • 50M uploads/day • 100:1 View-to-Upload Ratio.
Storage Reality: 50M videos × 100MB avg = 5 PB storage per day • 1.825 Exabytes per year!
Egress Bandwidth: 5B views × 100MB / 86,400s = 5.78 TB/sec (Must heavily utilize Global CDN edge caching).

nodes.name: Global Video CDN
nodes.why: Caches 95% of video chunks at edge

steps.description: 1. Ingestion: Creator uploads video directly to S3 Raw Bucket via Presigned URL.
2. S3 triggers event to Kafka Queue; Transcoding Worker pool encodes chunks into multiple bitrates.
3. Metadata saved in PostgreSQL with Redis caching.
4. Viewer requests video: 95% of chunks streamed directly from nearest Edge CDN PoP in 15ms.

topics.tradeoffs: Encoding videos synchronously during upload would cause 30-minute HTTP timeouts. Using an asynchronous worker pool with message queues decouples upload completion from encoding duration.

comparison_matrix.title: YouTube Read vs Write Pipeline Separation
rows: Upload Service + Kafka + GPU Transcoder Pool
Global Edge CDN + S3 Origin + Redis Metadata Cache
Client -> S3 Raw Bucket -> Transcoder -> S3 Chunks
Client -> Edge CDN -> (Cache Miss: S3 Chunks)

topics.failure_scenarios: Transcoding worker crashes halfway through a 2-hour 4K video encoding: without chunk-level checkpointing, the entire 2-hour job must restart. Solution: Chunk video into 4-second segments and encode chunks independently in parallel.

common_mistakes.mistake: Trying to stream video bytes through the PostgreSQL metadata database
common_mistakes.correction: Never store binary video files in relational databases. Store metadata (title, URL) in SQL and binary chunks in Object Storage (S3) served via CDN.

interview_questions.question: Why is Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (HLS / MPEG-DASH) crucial for platforms like YouTube?
interview_questions.answer: HLS breaks video into 4-second chunks encoded at multiple resolutions (360p to 4K). The client's video player dynamically monitors live network bandwidth on the fly: if mobile signal drops from 5G to 3G, the player seamlessly requests the next 4-second chunk at 480p instead of buffering.
